statusDefinitions.core: Implemented as part of the baseline shell/product surface and expected to be dependable for common use.
statusDefinitions.useful: Implemented with a practical in-process subset that is useful today; additional flags and edge cases may still be ported.
statusDefinitions.partial: Implemented or present, but intentionally limited enough that users should check command help, tests, or notes before relying on broad compatibility.
statusDefinitions.optional: Upstream-inspired feature that should only be available behind an explicit opt-in capability or runtime policy.
statusDefinitions.deferred: Tracked from the pinned upstream registry, but not implemented in gash yet.
statusDefinitions.unsupported: Known upstream feature that is intentionally not part of the current gash product surface.

commands.name: alias
commands.notes: Implemented by mvdan shell built-ins with expand_aliases enabled. Alias mutation/expansion is scoped to a single Exec; standalone internal command help is not provided.

commands.name: awk
commands.notes: First-class priority text command. Gash provides an in-process AWK subset with documented deferred language/runtime differences.

commands.name: bash
commands.notes: Handled by the gash interpreter rather than internal/commands.Builtins.

commands.name: cd
commands.notes: Shell built-in provided by the interpreter; it is not listed in the pinned just-bash command registry.

commands.name: chmod
commands.notes: Reports underlying virtual filesystem capability errors instead of rewriting all failures as missing files.

commands.name: cksum
commands.notes: Practical in-process POSIX CRC checksum and byte-count utility over stdin and virtual filesystem operands; broader non-POSIX implementation-specific flags are intentionally unsupported.

commands.name: cmp
commands.notes: In-process byte comparison with silent, verbose, byte-limit, initial-skip, positional skip, stdin, difference-location, and EOF behavior.

commands.name: curl
commands.notes: Implemented as an opt-in network command registered only when explicit Go API or CLI policy is supplied. Supports practical HTTP(S) methods, headers, auth, bodies/forms/uploads, redirects with revalidation, timeouts, verbose/write-out, virtual file input/output, bounded request/response sizes, and public-address DNS firewalling. Progress meters, proxies, netrc, TLS/client certificates, cookie-jar persistence, and full write-out variable parity are intentionally deferred.

commands.name: date
commands.notes: Supports common GNU-style output formats, -u/--utc, -d/--date parsing, and deterministic clock hooks; setting the system clock is unsupported.

commands.name: diff
commands.notes: First-class priority text command. Gash implements practical comparison and unified diff output; large-file hunk grouping may differ from upstream.

commands.name: egrep
commands.notes: Alias-style grep variant implemented by the gash grep handler.

commands.name: expr
commands.notes: First-class priority utility used by shell scripts; implemented with a practical expression subset.

commands.name: factor
commands.notes: In-process factorization of non-negative decimal integers up to 1000000000000. Reads argv or whitespace-separated stdin; zero and one are emitted with empty factor lists. Trial division is cancellation-aware.

commands.name: fgrep
commands.notes: First-class priority fixed-string grep variant implemented by the gash grep handler.

commands.name: find
commands.notes: First-class priority search command with capability-scoped -exec dispatch. Predicate truth propagation and action/traversal parity should expand with focused tasks.

commands.name: grep
commands.notes: Practical grep implementation; selected flags and variants are implemented in-process.

commands.name: gunzip
commands.notes: Implemented in-process for virtual filesystem and streams with gzip and ustar/pax tar create/list/extract support. Hostile extraction paths, unsafe links, and oversized archives are rejected; advanced tar/gzip flags and external codecs are intentionally deferred.

commands.name: gzip
commands.notes: Implemented in-process for virtual filesystem and streams with gzip and ustar/pax tar create/list/extract support. Hostile extraction paths, unsafe links, and oversized archives are rejected; advanced tar/gzip flags and external codecs are intentionally deferred.

commands.name: hash
commands.notes: Compatibility-only virtual command hash. hash -r resets an always-empty table as a no-op, and NAME resolution uses only shell built-ins and capability-scoped gash commands; host PATH entries are never resolved, cached, or reported.

commands.name: help
commands.notes: Standalone help lists registered gash commands and shows command-specific catalog entries.

commands.name: history
commands.notes: Registered for compatibility, but interactive history persistence is intentionally deferred; non-interactive gash reports an empty history.

commands.name: html-to-markdown
commands.notes: Implemented in-process with the Go HTML parser for common headings, paragraphs, emphasis, links/images, lists, blockquotes, and code blocks. Script/style content and unsafe javascript/data links are suppressed; exact upstream whitespace/plugins are intentionally deferred.

commands.name: id
commands.notes: Reports the fixed virtual identity user/1000 and primary group user/1000 without consulting host credentials, user databases, supplementary groups, or environment variables. Supports common user/group/name probes; user operands are unsupported.

commands.name: install
commands.notes: In-process virtual-filesystem subset supporting regular-file copies, executable-style mode 0755 by default, -m modes, -D parent creation, and -d directory creation. Ownership/group changes, stripping, SELinux contexts, and timestamp preservation are explicitly rejected.

commands.name: jq
commands.notes: Implemented as an in-process practical subset using gojq with JSON/raw/slurp/null input, raw/compact output, env and --arg/--argjson support, virtual file/stdin IO, and resource limits. Module/file loading, host execution, uncommon CLI flags, and exact jq diagnostics are intentionally deferred.

commands.name: js-exec
commands.notes: JavaScript execution is an optional runtime boundary and is not registered by gash today.

commands.name: ls
commands.notes: Supports directory operands, metadata-derived long modes, and conventional . and .. entries with -a; unsupported options are rejected.

commands.name: mktemp
commands.notes: Creates collision-resistant files and directories inside the virtual filesystem with -d, -p, --tmpdir, and trailing-X templates. Unlink, quiet, ownership, and suffix flags are intentionally unsupported.

commands.name: node
commands.notes: Node.js-compatible execution is an optional runtime boundary and is not registered by gash today.

commands.name: od
commands.notes: Supports -A address radices and c, o1, and x1 output types; unsupported options and types are rejected.

commands.name: paste
commands.notes: Registered in-process implementation with compatibility regression coverage.

commands.name: printf
commands.notes: Shell-oriented formatting includes Bash %q quoting and hexadecimal, octal, and Unicode \u/\U escapes in format strings and %b arguments; unsupported printf -v is rejected before execution.

commands.name: python
commands.notes: Python execution is an optional runtime boundary and is not registered by gash today.

commands.name: python3
commands.notes: Python execution is an optional runtime boundary and is not registered by gash today.

commands.name: realpath
commands.notes: Canonicalizes absolute virtual paths, follows virtual symlinks, and supports existing and missing-component modes without exposing host paths.

commands.name: rg
commands.notes: First-class priority search command. Gash searches the virtual filesystem with bounded in-process behavior and documented ripgrep differences.

commands.name: rm
commands.notes: Force mode suppresses missing-file errors only; capability and deletion failures remain visible and nonzero.

commands.name: sed
commands.notes: First-class priority stream editor. Gash implements a sandboxed subset and intentionally rejects shell-execution commands.

commands.name: sh
commands.notes: Handled by the gash interpreter rather than internal/commands.Builtins.

commands.name: sha512sum
commands.notes: In-process SHA-512 digest generation for virtual filesystem files and stdin; verification flags are not supported.

commands.name: shuf
commands.notes: In-process line randomization over stdin and virtual files, with bounded head counts, virtual numeric ranges, repeat mode, and operating-system cryptographic randomness. Unsupported GNU options are rejected.

commands.name: sort
commands.notes: Help lists only implemented options; common field separators and numeric key forms such as -t: -k2,2n are supported.

commands.name: sqlite3
commands.notes: Implemented in-process with modernc.org/sqlite (CGO-free) using virtual filesystem database image load/write-back, per-virtual-file locking, statement parsing, common sqlite3 output modes/options, and resource ceilings. Gash intentionally differs from just-bash by using Go context cancellation and SQLite limits instead of the sql.js worker protocol; ATTACH, VACUUM INTO, load_extension, and dot-command host escape paths are disabled.

commands.name: tar
commands.notes: Implemented in-process for virtual filesystem and streams with gzip and ustar/pax tar create/list/extract support. Hostile extraction paths, unsafe links, and oversized archives are rejected; advanced tar/gzip flags and external codecs are intentionally deferred.

commands.name: time
commands.notes: Runs commands through gash safe command dispatch and reports elapsed wall time; CPU accounting is zeroed.

commands.name: timeout
commands.notes: Runs commands through gash safe command dispatch with context cancellation; selected GNU timeout flags remain deferred.

commands.name: touch
commands.notes: Existing files require timestamp mutation capability; read-only filesystems return a nonzero error rather than a false success.

commands.name: type
commands.notes: Registered in-process discovery command supporting NAME..., -a, and -t. Discovery is deterministic and limited to shell built-ins, shell entry points, and the capability-scoped gash registry; host PATH lookup, executable paths, and Bash alias/function reporting are intentionally not supported.

commands.name: umask
commands.notes: Supports octal and rwx symbolic masks, -S/-p display, shell redirections, and in-process file creation.

commands.name: unalias
commands.notes: Implemented by mvdan shell built-ins and scoped to a single Exec.

commands.name: uname
commands.notes: Deterministic virtual platform identity: Gash, localhost, 1.0.0, #1 gash, and machine virtual. Processor, hardware-platform, and operating-system flags are intentionally unsupported.

commands.name: unlink
commands.notes: Additive gash file utility, not pinned just-bash parity. Removes exactly one non-directory path through the injected virtual filesystem and reports unsupported remove capabilities.

commands.name: uuidgen
commands.notes: Generates canonical lowercase RFC 4122 version-4 UUIDs using Go cryptographic randomness. Supports -r/--random; time- and MAC-based modes are intentionally unsupported.

commands.name: wc
commands.notes: Separate and clustered counter options accumulate and print in conventional line, word, character, byte order.

commands.name: which
commands.notes: Resolves only gash built-ins and shell entry points; host PATH executables are never reported.

commands.name: xan
commands.notes: Implemented as an in-process practical CSV subset supporting headers/columns, select, filter, sort, map, aggregate, groupby, multifile input, view output, UTF-8 data, and resource limits. Full xan expression language, reshape/join/statistical surface, and terminal styling are intentionally deferred.

commands.name: xargs
commands.notes: Implemented in-process with whitespace, custom, and NUL delimiters; replacement and argument batching, including attached -n1/-P2/-Ivalue/-dvalue forms; bounded parallel execution; verbose output; UTF-8 input; and safe virtual command dispatch. Full GNU quoting semantics and additional flags remain deferred.

commands.name: yes
commands.notes: Cancellation-aware in-process output generator bounded by the shared execution output limit.

commands.name: yq
commands.notes: Implemented as an in-process practical subset using gopkg.in/yaml.v3 plus gojq filters, supporting YAML stdin/files, multi-doc input, env navigation, JSON/raw output, UTF-8 data, and resource limits. Round-trip comments/styles, update-in-place, additional formats, and full yq CLI parity are intentionally deferred.

commands.name: zcat
commands.notes: Implemented in-process for virtual filesystem and streams with gzip and ustar/pax tar create/list/extract support. Hostile extraction paths, unsafe links, and oversized archives are rejected; advanced tar/gzip flags and external codecs are intentionally deferred.
